reconstructed_theorem_text: E_n=EuclideanSpace R (Fin(n+1)), the real (n+1)-coordinate space with its l2 Euclidean norm. Let S_n={z in E_n: ||z||=1}, considered as a subtype when it is used as a carrier. Let C_(n,N)=Fin N -> S_n. For a function a:S_n -> A into a type with a distinguished zero, write R(a)(z)=0 if z=0 and R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) otherwise; normalization is the first component of the supplied H. For A:E_n->E_n, coordinateDivergence A(z)=sum_(k in Fin(n+1)) lineDeriv_R (y -> (A(y))_k) z e_k, using the standard coordinate vectors e_k. The supplied trace formula is conditional on A being differentiable at z. Given V:Fin N->C_(n,N)->E_n, define at every x the sum over i:Fin N of coordinateDivergence(R(y -> V_i(update x i y)))(x_i). This is the exact target body: the ith component field is differentiated only in its own sphere coordinate with all others fixed, and then the results are added. No tangency, regularity or integrability is assumed. The N=0 value is the empty sum zero. This does not itself prove a divergence theorem or identify a separate covariant divergence.
